newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end firmer, helped by stock weakness.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end firmer, helped by stock weakness.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Monday, helped by gains in U.S. Treasuries, with fixed-income markets in both countries benefiting from initial weakness in equity markets.

"When the stock market goes down we seem to have higher bond prices. The stock market reaction on Friday certainly has created some flight to quality. We've seen some good interest in the short end of the curve," said David Yu, a fixed-income portfolio manager with Perigee Investment Counsel Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.24 to C$119.42 to yield 6.514 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 10/32 to yield 6.52 percent. The negative spread between the bonds was one basis point, unchanged from Friday's close.

Both Canadian and U.S. bonds were helped by an early deterioration in stock prices, which followed Friday's sharp selloff. Analysts said further losses in stocks encouraged investors to seek a safe haven in fixed-income markets, with the Canadian money market especially benefiting from the trend.
While U.S. stocks managed to rebound and end the session higher, Toronto stocks ended the day down.

Bond investors in both countries are now looking ahead to the release of U.S. housing starts data for July out tomorrow. Canadian fixed-income investors are also awaiting the release on Tuesday of the key consumer price index for July, which is expected to show the annual inflation rate in Canada remains below two percent.

Markets will also be watching for the outcome of a meeting tomorrow of the U.S. Federal Reserve's rate-setting Open Market Committee. The FOMC is widely expected to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.18 to C$109.55 to yield 5.946 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond rose 7/32 to yield 6.21 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds narrowed to 26 basis points from 32 basis points at Thursday's close.
The 10-year Canadian government bond futures contract trading on the Montreal Exchange closed up 0.52 to 120.37 with 2828 contracts changing hands, down from 3029 on Friday.
